title: Long-lived memory effects in the defect bath of superconducting qubits
authors: Abhishek Agarwal, Masum Uddin, Shroya Vaidya, Lachlan P. Lindoy, Ehsaneh Daghigh Ahmadi, Tobias Lindström, Sebastian E. de Graaf, Ivan Rungger
abstract: We reveal long-lived memory effects in the defect bath of a superconducting transmon qubit through electric-field tuning of two-level system (TLS) defects coupled to the qubit. Using a fast TLS mapping method we observe several hysteretic effects in the TLS environment with memory timescales of the order of seconds, far beyond the lifetimes of individual TLS defects. The observations can be explained by TLS coupling to electric field-polarised charge fluctuators in the defect bath. Our method enables detailed mapping of the dynamics of the bath's coupled microscopic degrees of freedom and the associated memory effects which can introduce temporally correlated noise. This information may be used to improve qubit-stabilisation and quantum error correction protocols.
summary: This paper experimentally reveals that superconducting transmon qubits suffer from memory effects caused by slow charge fluctuations within the material's defect bath. By tuning the electric field, the authors measured hysteretic changes in qubit decay rates with timescales reaching seconds. This work provides vital insights into non-Markovian noise sources, which is critical for advancing robust quantum computation.
main_problem: The study investigates long-lived memory effects originating from defect baths coupled to superconducting qubits, which introduce detrimental temporally correlated noise.
main_result: The research observed memory timescales on the order of seconds, significantly exceeding typical coherence times, attributed to coupling with electric field-polarized charge fluctuators (CFs).
method: The authors used electric-field tuning via a gate electrode and performed fast, repeated measurements of qubit relaxation probability ($P_e$) over extended laboratory time.
model_or_system: The physical system is a superconducting transmon qubit coupled to microscopic Two-Level System (TLS) defects. The memory effects are modeled by coupling the TLSs to electric field-polarized charge fluctuators (CFs).
key_observables: Qubit relaxation probability ($P_e$), hysteretic behavior in TLS resonance voltages, and sweep-rate dependence of $P_e$.
important_parameters: Memory timescales ($	au \sim$ seconds), electric field tuning voltage ($V_g$), and the characteristic equilibration time ($	au_{eq} \approx 5.4$ s).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the qubit transition frequency is insensitive to offset charge, and the CF model uses an approximation near the symmetry point.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental protocol, showing $P_e$ vs. sweep time over long lab times, comparing increasing/decreasing sweeps to reveal hysteresis, and demonstrating sweep-rate dependence of the measured probabilities.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental setup using electric-field tuning, presents measurements showing hysteretic behavior indicative of memory effects, models these effects using a charge-fluctuator approach, and quantifies the long equilibration times observed.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses noise sources in superconducting qubits by characterizing non-Markovian noise from defect baths, providing crucial data for improving qubit stabilization and quantum error correction protocols.
